title: Zombie To-Do List: (updated "post workflow" my "engine" will be spiting out fully packed games when I'm done training it) 🤣 — Everything top to bottom was done through prompting (besides creating the gist which I'm sure I can train it to do that to.)
author: Specialist_Chest7463

comments.author: dasjomsyeet
comments.body: So you made a prompt for text based games using LLMs, what exactly are you personally „training“ here? And how in the world will your model jump from writing basic text-game instructions to actually spitting out full games?

replies.author: Specialist_Chest7463
replies.body: im so glad you asked! I have made a prompt that is designed to 1. Brainstorming phases 2. Design phase 3. Test phase - so far and have started to use generative prompting patterns and self grading techniques all within the same project file so essential all I need to do is update the project instructions prompt to include a Game art and marketing phase and unless im missing a step in the gaming industry then I think it would be spitting out a full game not slop. That being said whether it be my current limitations with generative ai (99% chance thats the case) or its just the current limitations of the LLMs im choosing to wait to add that phase in completely until more training is provided to it this is the Second game it generated me i've chosen that not share the first one because it was truly slop lol

replies.author: Specialist_Chest7463
replies.body:
Everything and I mean everything was genuinely generated by ai in the main post all i did was describe the game i wanted in maybe 5 minutes of questions and another 5-10 minutes of editing outputs. 
Ive also got some nice little wording in the project instructions prompt to hopefully pick up on users personal tone, expressions, ideas, ect. When answering questions and try to implement it in the output soooo that being said making more games would help train the model (but there is more efficient not as fun ways to)
